spans.s:
√sthū, assumed as collateral form of sthā,
cf. sthávira, and see under √snā.

sthū́ṇā, f. post, pillar. [for *stul-na, fr.
√*stul or *stal, an extended form of
√*sta, Skt. sthā: cf. Ger. Stolle(n), Old
High Ger. stollo, *stol-no, ‘prop, post’;
στῦλ-ος, ‘post, pillar’; these words, like
στήλη, Doric στάλα, ‘prop, post,’ presuppose
the root in causal mgs, ‘cause to
stand,’ i. e. (a) ‘keep from falling, prop
up,’ and (b) ‘set up,’ as a pillar: the root
[]
appears also in Ger. Stall, Eng. stall,
‘stand, i. e. standing-place,’ and in Ger.
still, Eng. still, ‘standing, not moving.’]
